security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU implements the new mdtcfg CSR with incorrect WARL semantics — specifically, allowing writes to set SEDBGALW/VSEDBGALW/UEDBGALW/SETRCALW/VSETRCALW/UETRCALW fields to 1 even when the corresponding extension (Smsdedbg/Smvsdedbg/Smudedbg/Smsdetrc/Smvsdetrc/Smudetrc) is not implemented, or failing to preserve WPRI bits (5-7, 11-31 of mdtcfg) across read-modify-write sequences, violating the spec's requirement that unimplemented extension fields be read-only 0 and WPRI bits be preserved.
security_spec.summary: New mdtcfg CSR introduces 6 WARL debug/trace security control fields — QEMU must enforce read-only-zero for unimplemented extensions and preserve WPRI bits, or guest M-mode can unlock debug/trace access for privilege levels that should remain opaque to external debuggers

findings.finding: mdtcfg CSR is not implemented in this QEMU codebase. No WARL semantics, field masks, side-effects, TCG translation, KVM synchronization, migration state, reset values, or multi-hart indexing exist for this CSR. The target extensions (Smsdedbg/Smvsdedbg/Smudedbg/Smsdetrc/Smvsdetrc/Smudetrc) are absent from cpu_bits.h, csr.c, machine.c, and all other RISC-V emulation files. No privilege-escape vulnerability can exist for unimplemented CSR.
